A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Compute as Teacher and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original HealthBench and MATH-500 experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and output analyses in Section 4 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results, including model performance, judge sensitivity, rubric-conditioning ablations, and synthesis-output analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix F retain the same reference estimation, frozen anchor, self-proposed rubrics, reward derivation, GRPO training, and prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate healthcare responses on HealthBench and mathematical problem solving on MATH-500. No datasets, tasks, or distinct test scenarios are added or removed, including in the appendices.

E2.justification: The same physician-rubric, model-as-judge, CaT-SFT, majority-vote, Self-BoN, minimum-perplexity, and mutual-predictability comparisons remain in Sections 4.3–4.4 and Tables 3–6. The newly cited QA-LIGN work does not enter any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain the 500-example HealthBench test set, MATH-500 training and evaluation on the same 500 problems, eight rollouts, and the same models, metrics, training budgets, and stopping procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendices A–D retain the same analyses of synthesis disagreement, rubric conditioning, judge sensitivity, question omission, output structure, and learning plateaus. The worked example and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report standard errors across test samples, Welch’s t-tests in the figure captions, and seven-seed averaging for Table 1. No run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results, rankings, and qualitative findings match throughout, including Tables 1–9 and Figures 3–6. For example, Table 2 retains Gemma CaT scores of 0.43 ± 0.01 on HealthBench and 0.78 ± 0.02 on MATH-500.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their mathematical content remain unchanged, including reference estimation, rubric rewards, GRPO, perplexity, mutual predictability, and the SFT objective. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reference-free RL through self-proposed rubrics, amortizing inference-time aggregation into training, and applicability across non-verifiable and verifiable domains. The claimed performance and compute benefits are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of synthesis as reconciling complementary reasoning remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning base-model capability, judge quality, declining rollout diversity, and training plateaus.

D1.justification: Appendices F, H, and I retain the same prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, parsing instructions, and training details. The verl citation changes from Sheng et al. (2024) to its 2025 publication without changing the implementation or access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dineen et al. (2025), QA-LIGN, as support for the introduction’s existing statement about decomposed scoring. Other reference changes update publication metadata for retained works, such as Rubrics as Rewards, Tulu 3, and TTRL; the substantive research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises author-affiliation annotations, footnote symbols, the document date, citation years, and bibliographic metadata. Shashwat Goel’s direct Meta affiliation becomes a work-done-at-Meta footnote. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author header is rewrapped, and expanded references reflow across pages 9–11, with small text-flow adjustments elsewhere. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–12, and Algorithm 1 retain their content, display structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a supporting citation and updates affiliation and publication metadata, but leaves the scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility guidance unchanged. These limited attribution and layout edits do not meaningfully alter the paper’s overall clarity or evidential strength.
